sanskrit: yāvat tu niryatas tasya rajorūpam adṛśyata naivekṣvākuvaras tāvat saṃjahārātmacakṣuṣī
english: As long as the dust-cloud raised by his departure was visible, the lord of the Ikṣvākus kept his own eyes fixed upon it, unable to withdraw them.

sanskrit: yāvad rājā priyaṃ putraṃ paśyaty atyantadhārmikam tāvad vyavardhatevāsya dharaṇyāṃ putradarśane
english: As long as the king gazed upon his beloved and supremely righteous son, the earth seemed to swell and rise before him in the sight of that son.

sanskrit: na paśyati rajo 'py asya yadā rāmasya bhūmipaḥ tadārtaś ca viṣaṇṇaś ca papāta dharaṇītale
english: When the lord of the earth could no longer see even the dust of Rāma's chariot, stricken with grief and utterly desolate, he fell to the ground.

sanskrit: tasya dakṣiṇam anvagāt kausalyā bāhum aṅganā vāmaṃ cāsyānvagāt pārśvaṃ kaikeyī bharatapriyā
english: Kausalyā, that noble lady, supported his right arm, while Kaikeyī, dear to Bharata, supported his left side.

sanskrit: tāṃ nayena ca saṃpanno dharmeṇa nivayena ca uvāca rājā kaikeyīṃ samīkṣya vyathitendriyaḥ
english: The king, endowed with statecraft, righteousness, and propriety, looked at Kaikeyī and, his every sense tormented, spoke to her thus.

sanskrit: kaikeyi mā mamāṅgāni sprākṣīs tvaṃ duṣṭacāriṇī na hi tvāṃ draṣṭum icchāmi na bhāryā na ca bāndhavī
english: "Touch not my limbs, O Kaikeyī, you of wicked conduct! I have no wish to see you — you are neither wife nor kin to me."

sanskrit: ye ca tvām upajīvanti nāhaṃ teṣāṃ na te mama kevalārthaparāṃ hi tvāṃ tyaktadharmāṃ tyajāmy aham
english: "Those who depend upon you — I am not theirs, nor are they mine. You who have abandoned dharma in pursuit of mere self-interest — I renounce you."

sanskrit: agṛhṇāṃ yac ca te pāṇim agniṃ paryaṇayaṃ ca yat anujānāmi tat sarvam asmiṃl loke paratra ca
english: "Whatever vows I made when I took your hand, whatever acts I performed when we circled the sacred fire — I hereby release all of that, both in this world and the next."

sanskrit: bharataś cet pratītaḥ syād rājyaṃ prāpyedam avyayam yan me sa dadyāt pitrarthaṃ mā mā tad dattam āgamat
english: "If Bharata takes pleasure in this indestructible kingdom once he obtains it, let whatever he might offer on my behalf for my funerary rites never come to me."

sanskrit: atha reṇusamudhvastaṃ tam utthāpya narādhipam nyavartata tadā devī kausalyā śokakarśitā
english: Then Queen Kausalyā, wasted by grief, lifted up the lord of men who had been cast down and covered in dust, and turned back.

sanskrit: hatveva brāhmaṇaṃ kāmāt spṛṣṭvāgnim iva pāṇinā anvatapyata dharmātmā putraṃ saṃcintya tāpasaṃ
english: The righteous-souled king burned with remorse — as one who has slain a brahmin out of passion, as one who has touched sacred fire with bare hands — reflecting upon his ascetic son.

sanskrit: nivṛtyaiva nivṛtyaiva sīdato rathavartmasu rājño nātibabhau rūpaṃ grastasyāṃśumato yathā
english: Turning back again and again, sinking into despondency on the chariot-path, the king's form shone not at all — like the sun when it is swallowed up in eclipse.

sanskrit: vilalāpa ca duḥkhārtaḥ priyaṃ putram anusmaran nagarāntam anuprāptaṃ buddhvā putram athābravīt
english: Tormented by sorrow, recalling his beloved son, the king lamented; and understanding that his son had reached the outskirts of the city, he cried out.

sanskrit: vāhanānāṃ ca mukhyānāṃ vahatāṃ taṃ mamātmajam padāni pathi dṛśyante sa mahātmā na dṛśyate
english: "The hoofprints of the finest steeds that bore my son are still visible on the road, yet that great-souled one himself is nowhere to be seen."

sanskrit: sa nūnaṃ kva cid evādya vṛkṣamūlam upāśritaḥ kāṣṭhaṃ vā yadi vāśmānam upadhāya śayiṣyate
english: "Surely he will take shelter at the root of some tree this very night, and rest his head upon a log or a stone."

sanskrit: utthāsyati ca medinyāḥ kṛpaṇaḥ pāṃśuguṇṭhitaḥ viniḥśvasan prasravaṇāt kareṇūnām ivarṣabhaḥ
english: "And he will rise pitifully from the earth, smeared with dust, sighing deeply — like a great bull elephant rising from a stream."

sanskrit: drakṣyanti nūnaṃ puruṣā dīrghabāhuṃ vanecarāḥ rāmam utthāya gacchantaṃ lokanātham anāthavat
english: "The forest-dwellers will surely behold long-armed Rāma, the lord of the world, rising and walking as though he were lordless and without refuge."

sanskrit: sakāmā bhava kaikeyi vidhavā rājyam āvasa na hi taṃ puruṣavyāghraṃ vinā jīvitum utsahe
english: "Rejoice in your desire, O Kaikeyī! Rule the kingdom as a widow — for without that tiger among men, I cannot bring myself to live."

sanskrit: ity evaṃ vilapan rājā janaughenābhisaṃvṛtaḥ apasnāta ivāriṣṭaṃ praviveśa purottamam
english: Thus lamenting, the king, surrounded by a throng of people, entered that finest of cities — like one who has bathed without performing the obligatory rites after an ill omen.

sanskrit: śūnyacatvaraveśmāntāṃ saṃvṛtāpaṇadevatām klāntadurbaladuḥkhārtāṃ nātyākīrṇamahāpathām
english: Its crossroads and inner courts were deserted; its shops and shrines were shuttered; its people were weary, weak, and grief-stricken; its great thoroughfares were no longer crowded.

sanskrit: tām avekṣya purīṃ sarvāṃ rāmam evānucintayan vilapan prāviśad rājā gṛhaṃ sūrya ivāmbudam
english: Surveying the entire city and thinking only of Rāma, the lamenting king entered his palace as the sun enters a cloud.

sanskrit: mahāhradam ivākṣobhyaṃ suparṇena hṛtoragam rāmeṇa rahitaṃ veśma vaidehyā lakṣmaṇena ca
english: The palace, bereft of Rāma, of Vaidehī, and of Lakṣmaṇa, was like a great deep lake, once unagitated, whose serpent has been carried off by Suparṇa.

sanskrit: kausalyāyā gṛhaṃ śīghraṃ rāma mātur nayantu mām iti bruvantaṃ rājānam anayan dvāradarśitaḥ
english: "Take me quickly to the home of Kausalyā, Rāma's mother" — so saying, the king was led by the doorkeeper to her dwelling.

sanskrit: tatas tatra praviṣṭasya kausalyāyā niveśanam adhiruhyāpi śayanaṃ babhūva lulitaṃ manaḥ
english: Having entered Kausalyā's apartments and even having mounted his couch there, his mind remained utterly distraught.

sanskrit: tac ca dṛṣṭvā mahārājo bhujam udyamya vīryavān uccaiḥ svareṇa cukrośa hā rāghava jahāsi mām
english: Seeing that, the great king, valiant though he was, raised his arm and cried aloud in a loud voice: "Ah, Rāghava! You have abandoned me!"

sanskrit: sukhitā bata taṃ kālaṃ jīviṣyanti narottamāḥ pariṣvajanto ye rāmaṃ drakṣyanti punar āgatam
english: "Blessed indeed will those best of men be at that time — they shall live in happiness, embracing Rāma upon his return!"

sanskrit: na tvāṃ paśyāmi kausalye sādhu māṃ pāṇinā spṛśa rāmaṃ me 'nugatā dṛṣṭir adyāpi na nivartate
english: "I do not see you, Kausalyā — touch me kindly with your hand. My eyes have followed after Rāma and even now will not come back."

sanskrit: taṃ rāmam evānuvicintayantaṃ samīkṣya devī śayane narendram upopaviśyādhikam ārtarūpā viniḥśvasantī vilalāpa kṛcchraṃ
english: Seeing the lord of men lying on the couch thinking only of Rāma, the queen sat beside him, her form utterly overcome with anguish, and she lamented with sighs and great difficulty.

sanskrit: tataḥ samīkṣya śayane sannaṃ śokena pārthivam kausalyā putraśokārtā tam uvāca mahīpatim
english: Then Kausalyā, herself tormented by grief for her son, looked at the lord of the earth who had sunk upon his couch in sorrow, and spoke to the great king.

sanskrit: rāghavo naraśārdūla viṣam uptvā dvijihvavat vicariṣyati kaikeyī nirmukteva hi pannagī
english: "O tiger among men, Kaikeyī, having sown her poison like a two-tongued serpent, will now roam freely — like a serpent that has shed its skin."

sanskrit: vivāsya rāmaṃ subhagā labdhakāmā samāhitā trāsayiṣyati māṃ bhūyo duṣṭāhir iva veśmani
english: "Having exiled Rāma, that fortunate woman has achieved her desire and, composed, will continue to terrify me again and again — like a vicious serpent within the house."

sanskrit: atha sma nagare rāmaś caran bhaikṣaṃ gṛhe vaset kāmakāro varaṃ dātum api dāsaṃ mamātmajam
english: "Better it would have been for Rāma to remain in the city begging for alms and living in our home than to grant his stepmother's wish — even if it meant his becoming her servant."

sanskrit: pātayitvā tu kaikeyyā rāmaṃ sthānād yatheṣṭataḥ pradiṣṭo rakṣasāṃ bhāgaḥ parvaṇīvāhitāgninā
english: "Having toppled Rāma from his rightful place as she desired, Kaikeyī has assigned the share — as it were — to the rākṣasas, like sacrificial oblations cast into fire at a lunar rite."

sanskrit: gajarājagatir vīro mahābāhur dhanurdharaḥ vanam āviśate nūnaṃ sabhāryaḥ sahalakṣmaṇaḥ
english: "That hero with the gait of a lordly elephant, long-armed, bearing his bow — surely he has entered the forest now, accompanied by his wife and together with Lakṣmaṇa."

sanskrit: vane tv adṛṣṭaduḥkhānāṃ kaikeyyānumate tvayā tyaktānāṃ vanavāsāya kā nv avasthā bhaviṣyati
english: "By your consent to Kaikeyī's command, you have abandoned to forest-exile those who have never known hardship — what will become of them in the forest?"

sanskrit: te ratnahīnās taruṇāḥ phalakāle vivāsitāḥ kathaṃ vatsyanti kṛpaṇāḥ phalamūlaiḥ kṛtāśanāḥ
english: "Those tender ones, stripped of every gem and jewel, banished in the fruiting season — how will they live pitifully, subsisting on fruit and roots?"

sanskrit: apīdānīṃ sa kālaḥ syān mama śokakṣayaḥ śivaḥ sabhāryaṃ yat saha bhrātrā paśyeyam iha rāghavam
english: "Will that auspicious time ever come — the end of my grief — when I may behold Rāghava here once more, together with his wife and his brother?"

sanskrit: śrutvaivopasthitau vīrau kadāyodhyā bhaviṣyati yaśasvinī hṛṣṭajanā sūcchritadhvajamālinī
english: "On the very news of those two heroes' arrival — when will Ayodhyā again be glorious, its people rejoicing, adorned with tall raised banners?"

sanskrit: kadā prekṣya naravyāghrāv araṇyāt punarāgatau nandiṣyati purī hṛṣṭā samudra iva parvaṇi
english: "When, beholding those two tigers among men returned from the forest, will the city rejoice with delight — as the ocean rejoices at the full moon?"

sanskrit: kadāyodhyāṃ mahābāhuḥ purīṃ vīraḥ pravekṣyati puraskṛtya rathe sītāṃ vṛṣabho govadhūm iva
english: "When will that long-armed hero enter the city of Ayodhyā, placing Sītā before him on the chariot — as a bull leads the cow at his side?"

sanskrit: kadā prāṇisahasrāṇi rājamārge mamātmajau lājair avakariṣyanti praviśantāv ariṃdamau
english: "When will thousands of living beings strew parched grain upon those two tamers of enemies, my sons, as they enter along the royal road?"

sanskrit: kadā sumanasaḥ kanyā dvijātīnāṃ phalāni ca pradiśantyaḥ purīṃ hṛṣṭāḥ kariṣyanti pradakṣiṇam
english: "When will the maidens, bearing flowers and the fruits of the twice-born, cheerfully circumambulate the city in their joy?"

sanskrit: kadā pariṇato buddhyā vayasā cāmaraprabhaḥ abhyupaiṣyati dharmajñas trivarṣa iva māṃ lalan
english: "When will he — matured in wisdom and in years, radiant as the cāmara white yak-tail fan — he who knows dharma, approach me playfully as if he were a child of three?"

sanskrit: niḥsaṃśayaṃ mayā manye purā vīra kadaryayā pātu kāmeṣu vatseṣu mātṝṇāṃ śātitāḥ stanāḥ
english: "Doubtless, O hero, I believe that in a former life I must have cruelly severed, out of wretched selfishness, the breasts of mother animals from their suckling young."

sanskrit: sāhaṃ gaur iva siṃhena vivatsā vatsalā kṛtā kaikeyyā puruṣavyāghra bālavatseva gaur balāt
english: "And now I, loving and devoted, have been made childless — like a cow bereft of her calf by a lion, O tiger among men — as Kaikeyī has forcibly taken my young calf."

sanskrit: na hi tāvad guṇair juṣṭaṃ sarvaśāstraviśāradam ekaputrā vinā putram ahaṃ jīvitum utsahe
english: "For I, who have but one son — one so endowed with virtues and learned in all the śāstras — I cannot bring myself to live without my son."

sanskrit: na hi me jīvite kiṃ cit sāmartham iha kalpyate apaśyantyāḥ priyaṃ putraṃ mahābāhuṃ mahābalam
english: "For me, not seeing my beloved son — long-armed and of great strength — there is no reason for this life to continue."

sanskrit: ayaṃ hi māṃ dīpayate samutthitas tanūjaśokaprabhavo hutāśanaḥ mahīm imāṃ raśmibhir uttamaprabho yathā nidāghe bhagavān divākaraḥ
english: "This fire of grief for my son, having arisen, consumes me — as the blessed sun in the hot season scorches this earth with his blazing rays."

sanskrit: vilapantīṃ tathā tāṃ tu kausalyāṃ pramadottamām idaṃ dharme sthitā dharmyaṃ sumitrā vākyam abravīt
english: But as that foremost of noble women Kausalyā lamented thus, Sumitrā — herself steadfast in dharma — spoke to her these words befitting dharma.

sanskrit: tavārye sadguṇair yuktaḥ putraḥ sa puruṣottamaḥ kiṃ te vilapitenaivaṃ kṛpaṇaṃ ruditena vā
english: "O noble lady, your son is endowed with all good qualities — that best of men. What purpose is served by your lamenting thus, by your pitiful weeping?"

sanskrit: yas tavārye gataḥ putras tyaktvā rājyaṃ mahābalaḥ sādhu kurvan mahātmānaṃ pitaraṃ satyavādinām
english: "O noble lady, your son of great might has gone — having renounced the kingdom — doing right by his great-souled father who had given his word in truth."

sanskrit: śiṣṭair ācarite samyak śaśvat pretya phalodaye rāmo dharme sthitaḥ śreṣṭho na sa śocyaḥ kadā cana
english: "Rāma stands firm in that dharma which the virtuous have ever rightly practiced, which yields its fruit in the life beyond — he is the foremost of men and is never to be mourned."

sanskrit: vartate cottamāṃ vṛttiṃ lakṣmaṇo 'smin sadānaghaḥ dayāvān sarvabhūteṣu lābhas tasya mahātmanaḥ
english: "And Lakṣmaṇa, ever sinless and compassionate toward all beings, serves that great-souled one in the noblest manner — he has gained great good fortune through this."

sanskrit: araṇyavāse yad duḥkhaṃ jānatī vai sukhocitā anugacchati vaidehī dharmātmānaṃ tavātmajam
english: "Vaidehī, though accustomed to comfort and well aware of the hardships of forest life, follows your son, the soul of righteousness — this too speaks of his greatness."

sanskrit: kīrtibhūtāṃ patākāṃ yo loke bhrāmayati prabhuḥ damasatyavrataparaḥ kiṃ na prāptas tavātmajaḥ
english: "The lord who waves as his banner throughout the world the flag that is his very glory, who is devoted to self-restraint, truth, and sacred vows — what has your son not already attained?"

sanskrit: vyaktaṃ rāmasya vijñāya śaucaṃ māhātmyam uttamam na gātram aṃśubhiḥ sūryaḥ saṃtāpayitum arhati
english: "Knowing Rāma's purity and his supreme greatness, the sun himself surely would not dare to scorch his body with his rays."

sanskrit: śivaḥ sarveṣu kāleṣu kānanebhyo viniḥsṛtaḥ rāghavaṃ yuktaśītoṣṇaḥ seviṣyati sukho 'nilaḥ
english: "Auspicious at all times, blowing forth from the forest groves, the gentle wind — pleasantly cool, neither too cold nor too warm — will attend upon Rāghava."

sanskrit: śayānam anaghaṃ rātrau pitevābhipariṣvajan raśmibhiḥ saṃspṛśañ śītaiś candramā hlādayiṣyati
english: "As Rāma sleeps at night, the moon — embracing the sinless one as a father would — will refresh him, touching him with its cool rays."

sanskrit: dadau cāstrāṇi divyāni yasmai brahmā mahaujase dānavendraṃ hataṃ dṛṣṭvā timidhvajasutaṃ raṇe
english: "And Brahmā himself bestowed divine weapons upon him of great might, having seen him slay in battle Timi's banner-son, the lord of the Dānavas."

sanskrit: pṛthivyā saha vaidehyā śriyā ca puruṣarṣabhaḥ kṣipraṃ tisṛbhir etābhiḥ saha rāmo 'bhiṣekṣyate
english: "That bull among men, Rāma, will soon be consecrated together with these three — the earth, Vaidehī, and royal Śrī — as his companions."

sanskrit: duḥkhajaṃ visṛjanty asraṃ niṣkrāmantam udīkṣya yam samutsrakṣyasi netrābhyāṃ kṣipram ānandajaṃ payaḥ
english: "The tears of sorrow you now shed gazing upon him as he departed — from those same eyes you will quickly shed tears of joy."

sanskrit: abhivādayamānaṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvā sasuhṛdaṃ sutam mudāśru mokṣyase kṣipraṃ meghalekeva vārṣikī
english: "Seeing your son bow to you in greeting, surrounded by his beloved companions, you will quickly shed tears of gladness — like a rain-cloud of the monsoon season."

sanskrit: putras te varadaḥ kṣipram ayodhyāṃ punar āgataḥ karābhyāṃ mṛdupīnābhyāṃ caraṇau pīḍayiṣyati
english: "Your boon-granting son will swiftly return to Ayodhyā and press your feet with his own soft and full hands."

sanskrit: niśamya tal lakṣmaṇamātṛvākyaṃ rāmasya mātur naradevapatnyāḥ sadyaḥ śarīre vinanāśa śokaḥ śaradgato megha ivālpatoyaḥ
english: Hearing those words of Lakṣmaṇa's mother, spoken to the mother of Rāma, the queen consort of the lord of men — immediately the grief in her body dissolved, like an autumn cloud diminished of its water.
